title: The Pronoun 'I' in the Divine Nature
english: Homily on 'I go': [By] Cyril, Bishop of Jerusalem, on the [words] 'I go to my Father; and whatever you ask in my name, I will do it, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son' (John 14:14).

Concerning both that which is said about the divinity and that which is said about the humanity, he sets forth the 'I', so as to show the intention of the words from their sequence, and the distinction of the natures from the difference of the things said. And from the debating in both ways, he signifies the connection of the person regarding one single thing.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
